context: The user asks for the JSON error response body for a payouts endpoint with three distinct failure modes (expired bank token, daily limit exceeded, third-party vendor rejection). The criteria check whether the design follows the skill's error-handling conventions — a unified issues array, namespaced string codes with no separate type field, correlation metadata, and a dedicated structure for third-party errors — without those conventions being stated in the task.

checklist.name: Unified issues array
checklist.description: The response uses a single `issues` array with one entry per failure, not separate `errors`/`warnings` arrays or a single top-level error object

checklist.name: Namespaced dot-string issue codes
checklist.description: Each issue carries a single namespaced code in `{domain}.{class}.{reason}` form (e.g. `payout.unauthorized.token_expired`), not numeric or flat strings

checklist.name: No separate type field
checklist.description: Issue objects do NOT include a separate `type` field alongside the namespaced `code` — the class is parsed from the code itself

checklist.name: Severity present
checklist.description: Each issue includes a `severity` field (e.g. error/warning)

checklist.name: correlationId present
checklist.description: The response includes a `correlationId` for debugging

checklist.name: Third-party error surfaced via object
checklist.description: The Sequra (vendor) rejection is surfaced via a dedicated `thirdParty` object that carries the vendor's own code, rather than being flattened into the top-level issue code

checklist.name: Descriptive string codes not numeric
checklist.description: Codes are descriptive strings, not opaque numeric codes

checklist.name: Message and links where useful
checklist.description: Issues include a human-readable `message` and/or `links` for at least some failures
